documents.t: Workspace-operation history is short-lived on purpose. Each table has its own 50-entry bucket while this browser tab keeps the workspace page mounted. Switching among Table, Details, and Relations keeps the bucket. Visiting another table switches to that table's bucket, and returning restores the first table's bucket. Appearance, Publish, and Media leave the bucket in place but cannot apply it. Reloading the page, closing the tab, opening the workspace in a new tab, or completing a type conversion that rewrites stored cells starts workspace-operation history fresh. A new edit after Undo clears the redo path, as in other editors. The separate view history also starts fresh when you move to another saved view or table or reload, while the saved view itself keeps the arrangement durably.
documents.s: When the undo history starts over

documents.t: Open a table without naming a view in the address, and the table's shared default view is the starting point. That default includes its view kind — for example, a table can open directly in Table or Details if that is the default view's mode. The browser you are using can also remember a concrete non-default view you opened in that table. That memory is kept per table, in that browser — a different computer, a different browser, or a private window starts fresh. It does not turn the default view into a private personal default. Two things always win over this memory: An explicit link. A view link a colleague sends you opens exactly the view in the link, not your remembered one. The shared default. If no concrete saved-view link or remembered concrete view applies, the workspace uses the table's default view and its view kind. A removed view. If the view you last used no longer exists, the workspace falls back to the table's default view. The sidebar's size is browser-side memory too: its width, and whether you collapsed it to the icon rail, are restored the next time you open the workspace in the same browser. Some things are deliberately not remembered: the toolbar's quick filter text and your row selection clear when you move to another table or view, so you never land on yesterday's narrowing without noticing.
documents.s: What the browser you are using remembers

documents.t: How you organized the sidebar — pinned tables, named groups, the order of your tables, which groups you collapsed, and your recently opened tables — is stored with your sign-in for this environment rather than in the browser. Resizing the sidebar stays with the browser; organizing it stays with you.

Saved views are shared — everyone in your environment sees the same view tabs. Which tab you land on can still differ when one browser follows a concrete view link or remembers a concrete non-default view, while another browser starts from the table's default. You are both looking at the same shared set of views, opened at different tabs. To get back to the shared starting point, select the default view — the first tab in the view tab row. Each table has exactly one default view; Set as default in a view tab's menu changes which view that is, for everyone.
documents.s: Why you and a colleague may not see the same view

documents.t: Symptom Likely cause Fix Workspace Undo is grayed out. The active table has no reversible edit in this browser tab, or an undo/redo is still applying. Finish the current editor or wait for replay to finish. If you reloaded or opened a new tab, reapply the change by hand. Undo refused instead of changing a value or field. The current value or field definition no longer matches the recorded operation, so replay would overwrite newer work. Review the current state and decide which edit should win; then make that edit deliberately. A removed relationship was not restored. The restore was already used, is older than 90 days, would duplicate an existing link, belongs to another person or environment, or the relationship field no longer permits it. Refresh Relations and review the current rule and links. Add the link again only if the current configuration allows it. Ctrl/Cmd+Z did nothing in Appearance, Publish, or Media. Workspace-history shortcuts are intentionally inactive on non-editing surfaces. Return to Table, Details, or Relations to undo a record, field, paste, row-order, or relationship edit. Undo did not reverse a publish, visibility, privacy, citation, media, import, row-create, or field-create action. Those operations are outside workspace edit history. Use that surface's explicit controls or correction process. Workspace Undo never changes publication or privacy state. The workspace opened on a different view than your colleague sees. One of you followed a concrete view link or had a remembered concrete view; the other started from the shared default. Select the same view tab, or open the same view link. The workspace did not return you to your last view. You opened a link that names a view, you are in a different browser or a private window, the remembered view was removed, or the shared default view is taking precedence. Open the view's tab again, or ask your team which view should be the default. The sidebar looks different on another computer. Sidebar width and collapse are remembered per browser; only its organization follows your account. Resize or collapse the sidebar once on the new computer — your groups, pins, and table order are already with your account. A deleted view is not in either history. Saved-view deletion is confirmed rather than undoable, and it removes the view for everyone in the environment. Recreate the view, and next time Duplicate a shared view before experimenting on it.

Workspace walkthrough — every control mentioned here: views, filters, columns, the command palette. Adding and editing rows — how record values are edited and saved. Accessibility — density mode and other display-comfort controls.

The workspace is the table of records of one type — figures, terms, manuscript editions, anything your project tracks — wrapped in a toolbar, a left sidebar, and a set of view tabs. This page walks through what is on the screen, what each control does, and what a typical session looks like. Read it when you first open the workspace, when a control is doing something you did not expect, or when you want to set up a view you can come back to.

Workspace layout (Active) — every table opens in the same shell: a left sidebar listing your tables, a top bar with search and the command palette, a toolbar of table controls, and view tabs that switch between Table, Details, Relations, and Publish. Workspace search (Active) — a quick search panel that finds records across the workspace, grouped by table. Results respect your permissions. When search cannot run, the panel says workspace search is unavailable rather than showing empty results. Search & Read section (Active) — a full search page with a typeahead, an advanced field-condition filter, paged results, and a reading pane that opens a record beside the list. The page address encodes the whole search, so it can be shared or bookmarked. Rows named by your row-title field (Active) — Details, Relations, and Publish use the collection's configured title value for each record. A row without that value stays visibly unnamed rather than inheriting a generic record-type label or a guessed field. Sidebar organizer and command palette (Active) — pin tables, create named groups, collapse or expand groups, see your recently opened tables, and reset the sidebar to its defaults. The command palette reaches all of these without leaving the keyboard. Current-table quick filter (Active) — a toolbar box that narrows the active table to the rows in the whole collection that contain a typed term. It is not a whole-workspace search. Filters (Active) — composable filter conditions per field. The filter options match the field's type: text fields match typed text, number and year fields take a number, Date fields open a date picker, and choice fields offer their options. Active filters appear as removable chips. Column manager (Active) — reorder, show or hide, search columns, and choose the display column; resize by dragging column edges in the table, and pin columns from the column header menu. Saved views (Active) — named tabs that remember filters, sort, column layout, density, and row colors. Views belong to the table and are shared with everyone who works in your environment. Per-view sharing permissions are not yet available. Density toggle (Active) — compact, cozy, or comfortable row height, remembered per view. Record panel (Active) — open any record to see every field with its editor, related records, and a preview of the saved public page. Fields composed from other fields are labeled read-only — they cannot be edited directly. Clipboard and selected-row export (Active) — copy one cell, a rectangular cell range, or targeted individual cells. Select rows, then use Export in the table toolbar to download CSV or raw JSON. Copy view link (Active) — copies a URL that opens the same view for a collaborator, subject to their own permissions. Editing history across views (Active) — Table, Details, and Relations share one per-table history for values, paste, manual row order, field definitions, and relationships. Appearance, Publish, and Media do not intercept its shortcuts.

Your knowledge environment has a sidebar listing the record types you can work with. Click one and you land in its workspace at /app/workspace/<record-type>/. You can bookmark and share the URL. If your project has several record types, each has its own workspace.

Find a record across the workspace. Click Search database… in the top bar, or press Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F. Type at least two characters. Choose Current table when you know the table, or All workspace when you do not — and in workspace scope you can still narrow to one table with the Table selector. Results are grouped by table; move with the arrow keys and press Enter, or click a result to open that record. The panel's Filter current table button hands your search words to the table's quick filter instead. When you want to browse and read many records at once, Open full Search & Read in the panel — or Search & Read in the command palette — opens the full search page, carrying your words over; see Searching and reading. Organize the left sidebar. Pin the tables you use most, gather tables into named groups, and collapse the groups you are not using. Recent lists the tables you opened last. Useful shortcuts: Ctrl/Cmd+K opens the command palette, Ctrl/Cmd+B collapses the sidebar to an icon rail, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+G creates a group, and Shift+S pins or unpins the current table. Reset sidebar to default groups in the command palette puts everything back. Filter the table in front of you. Use the toolbar Filter rows box to narrow the active table to the matching rows from its whole collection. This quick filter is transient and is not stored with the view. Add filters to narrow. Click Filter and pick a field. The options match the field's type — type a word for text fields, type a number for numeric fields, pick a calendar date for Date fields, or pick options for choice fields. A Date filter matches stored timestamps that fall on the same calendar date; a field that only looks like a timestamp but is still configured as Text keeps text-style matching. The match count updates as you set the condition. Filter chips appear in the toolbar after the "filtering by" lead-in. They compose. Remove a chip by clicking its ×; remove all of them with Clear. Tidy the columns. Click Columns to open the column manager: drag entries to reorder, uncheck columns to hide them, search by label or field key, and choose the display column. Resize a column by dragging its edge in the table itself. Pinning and wrap-text controls live in each column's header menu. Save the arrangement as a view. Views are the tabs above the table. Click + Add view, give it a name like "18th-century figures with manuscript citations", and it starts from your current arrangement. From then on, changes you make while that view is active — filters, sort, columns, density — are stored on the view as you go. Undo view change and Redo view change step those presentation changes backward and forward. Open a record. Click the row's Open details button (at the row's actions end) and the record panel opens over the table: every field with its editor, related records, and a preview of the saved public page. Close it with the × in its header, with Escape, or by clicking outside it. Edit in the table. Double-click a cell to edit it. Short values save when you press Enter or move away; larger editors — long text, formatted text — have their own Save and Cancel buttons. Empty cells show empty so blanks are visible without looking like punctuation. Date fields use a date picker and display readable dates; text fields that contain timestamp-shaped strings stay raw text until the field type is changed or converted. If a value cannot be saved, the workspace tells you rather than silently dropping it. Undo an edit from where you are. In Table, Details, or Relations, the workspace-history controls name the next operation and where it came from. Use Ctrl/Cmd+Z to undo; redo with Ctrl/Cmd+Y or Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+Z. Saved-view presentation has its own separate Undo/Redo actions. See What the workspace remembers — and what you can undo.
documents.s: The default flow: search, filter, open, edit

documents.t: Switch to the Details tab. It splits the screen: a list of the table's records on one side and the full record on the other. The list uses each record's configured row title; a missing title stays visibly unnamed. Click through the list and the record pane follows; the list can be narrowed with its own filter box, so you can audit a slice or fact-check a draft against its neighbors without losing your place.

Focus a row and press Space to select it. Use Ctrl/Cmd+Space to add or remove the focused row, and Shift with the arrow keys to extend the selection through a range. In the table toolbar, choose Export, then select Download CSV for a spreadsheet-friendly file or Download raw JSON for the raw row payload. For cells rather than full rows, click a cell, drag or Shift-extend a rectangle, or turn on Target cells for non-adjacent cells. Cell copy uses only the cell values in the range or targeted set.
Click Copy link in the toolbar, or Copy view link in a view tab's menu. Paste the URL into chat or email. Your collaborator opens it and lands on the same view, subject to their own permissions.
documents.s: Sharing a view with a collaborator

documents.t: A saved view remembers filters and their values, sort order, column layout (order, widths, pinning, hidden columns), row density, and row color rules. It does not remember the quick-filter text — that stays per-session so you do not accidentally land on yesterday's search. Views belong to the table, not to you alone: everyone working in your environment sees the same view tabs, and changes to a view reach your collaborators too. Each view's tab menu offers Rename, Duplicate, Pin view, Set as default (the view the table opens with), Copy view link, and Delete view. Deleting a view removes it for everyone, so agree with your collaborators first — Duplicate is the safe way to experiment on a shared view.
documents.s: What saved views remember (and how they are shared)

documents.t: Symptom Likely cause Fix Where to escalate A control mentioned here is missing or grayed out. The control depends on your role, or on a capability not yet available — grayed controls often say "Backend pending". Hover the control; its tooltip states the reason. Contact your environment administrator. Columns you arranged reverted later. The changes were made outside a saved view, so nothing stored them. Click + Add view, name it, and arrange columns while that view is active — changes then stick. n/a Search returns matches in an unexpected language or script form. The field stores several language or script forms, and search matches any of them. This is the intended behavior; see Searching and reading. Contact your environment administrator if matching is wrong for your project. The top search finds a row but the toolbar box does not. They are different tools: the top search looks across the workspace, while the toolbar box answers only for the collection in the current table. Open the result from the top search, or switch to the right table before using the toolbar filter. n/a The search panel says workspace search is unavailable. Your role does not include workspace search, or the search request failed. Try the search again. The toolbar filter box answers through the same engine, so if it also reports "Filter unavailable", search is not enabled for this workspace. Contact your environment administrator. Editing a cell does nothing. The field is read-only — composed fields, for example, cannot be edited directly — or the value was rejected. Open the record panel and check the field there; rejected values show a message instead of saving silently. Contact your environment administrator about permissions. The record panel will not close. A confirmation dialog is open and is catching the Escape key. Dismiss the dialog first, then press Escape. n/a
